endorsements.quote: Authors should therefore report how and when generative AI was used in the research or writing process, specifying the tools, the nature of the AI-generated content, and, where relevant, the prompts that shaped it [ 39 ], per guidelines developed by JMIR leadership.

Reporting frameworks such as CONSORT-AI (Consolidated Standards of Reporting Trials–Artificial Intelligence), SPIRIT-AI (Standard Protocol Items: Recommendations for Interventional Trials–Artificial Intelligence), DECIDE-AI (Developmental and Exploratory Clinical Investigations of Decision Support Systems Driven by Artificial Intelligence), MI-CLAIM (Minimum Information About Clinical Artificial Intelligence Modeling), MINIMAR (Minimum Information for Medical AI Reporting), TRIPOD-AI (Transparent Reporting of a Multivariable Prediction Model for Individual Prognosis or Diagnosis–Artificial Intelligence), and AI model cards published by developers can help authors describe AI systems with better precision.

unlisted_practices: Specify the human support roles in AI studies, including who performs them, their training, what data they monitor, and when they intervene.

Do not treat human-in-the-loop as a safety claim unless the loop is described in enough detail to show who is responsible, what they can see, when they act, and what authority they have to change care.
Clearly define adverse event criteria, specify monitoring protocols, identify escalation thresholds, and transparently report safety findings in digital mental health trials.

Evaluate AI mental health tools using clinically meaningful real-world outcomes such as functional improvement, quality of life, safety, and integration into care pathways, rather than only simulated cases or benchmarks.
Characterize the AI technology under study precisely, distinguishing base model, wrapper or interface, system prompt, safety guardrails, and deployment context.
Use comparators and controls that account for the nonspecific effects of digital technology when evaluating digital mental health interventions.
Evaluate AI tools across multiple models, versions, settings, or populations so that findings remain useful as technologies change.
Assess whether the language, culture, infrastructure, costs, literacy, and care pathways assumed by an AI tool fit the intended user group and population.

Ensure real-world data used in AI evaluation are appropriate for the research question, including sample size and representativeness, and account for engagement, outcomes, covariates, and confounders.
Do not conduct AI research that uses patient data without appropriate permissions.
